test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: maths
question: The height of a solid cylinder is 35 cm. The circumference of its base is 37 cm more than the radius. What will be the volume of this cylinder ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the ratio of Circumference to Radius is 2π : 1, which is approximately 44/7 : 1.

The difference (Circumference − Radius) = 44/7 − 1 = 37/7 units.

According to the question: 37/7 units = 37 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 7 cm.

So, the radius (r) = 7 cm.

Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 7 × 7 × 35 = 154 × 35 = 5390 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 5390 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Height of cylinder (h) = 35 cm

Circumference of base − Radius = 37 cm

Formula used:

Circumference of base = 2πr

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b839dc7a7d1f7f8bca07c3f2f97134b42df38f5d942982ee074821daa2eb092d.png] 

Step 1: Find the radius (r) using the base property.

⇒ 2πr − r = 37

⇒ r(2π − 1) = 37

⇒ r(2 × 22/7 − 1) = 37

⇒ r(44/7 − 1) = 37

⇒ r(37/7) = 37

⇒ r = 37 × 7/37

⇒ r = 7 cm

Step 2: Calculate the volume of the cylinder.

⇒ Volume = π × r² × h

⇒ Volume = 22/7 × 7 × 7 × 35

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 35

⇒ Volume = 154 × 35

⇒ Volume = 5390 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5390 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of Cylinder

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) is 2πrh and the Total Surface Area (TSA) is 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone with the same base radius and height is exactly one-third of the cylinder: V = 1/3 × πr²h.

Circle Constants

For a circle with radius 7, the circumference is 44 and the area is 154. These are useful benchmarks for fast calculations.</p
